Forecast Discussion

High pressure over the Tennessee Valley keeps the mountains dry today, with light northwest winds and another pleasant afternoon after a frosty start in the valleys.

Subtropical Storm Josephine is now a named storm well east of New Jersey. Jo Jo developed from the system that sat off the Northeast coast most of the week. It pulls away toward Newfoundland today and Friday. Jo Jo has no direct effect on our weather, but along with high pressure building into Pennsylvania and New York, cool, dry air is directed down the east side of the Appalachians Friday. This cool wedge holds through the weekend. Friday is a few degrees cooler; Saturday is the coolest day.

The high settles over the Carolinas Monday and Tuesday, giving us a slow “mild up” early next week.

The next period of showers? Around the night of November 1 into November 2.
